headline: Zoning change for 76 Congress Street, $900,000 and $350,000 winter warming shelter funding, and sale of Portland Technology Park Units 3 and 5.
summary: The agenda includes two winter warming shelter funding orders and a limited emergency declaration at 654 Riverside Street. It also covers a Technology Park land sale, a Northeast Air lease extension, and changes to parking and traffic rules.

Special Meeting of the Corporator of the Portland Development Corporation 
 
Order 71-26/27 Amending  the Portland Development Corporation's Business 
Assistance Program for Job Creation Guidelines - Sponsored by Danielle P. West, 
City Manager 
    
  
At the Portland Development Corporation (PDC) Board of Directors meeting held on 
October 15, 2026, the Board voted 6-0 to recommend to the City Council approval of the 
proposed amendments to the Business Assistance Grant Program for job creation 
guidelines. 
 
In June 2025, the PDC’s application for CDBG funding to provide funding for the 
Business Assistance for Job Creation grant program was approved as part of the FY25-26 
HUD Award to the City, and City Council approved program guidelines in July 2025. 
Those guidelines limited grants to $10,000 per grantee and restricted eligible uses to 
commercial rent to encourage activation of commercial spaces. Implementation of this 
program has since been delayed by the inclusion of HUD Addendum 1, and staff have
2 
only recently begun programming the funds. All funds must be expended by June 30, 
2027. 
 
To enable the programming of these funds as quickly as possible, the PDC Board voted to 
recommend to the City Council approval of the proposed amendments to the grant 
guidelines to allow grants of up to $20,000 ($10,000 per full-time job equivalent created), 
and to expand eligible activities beyond rent to include additional working capital costs 
such as payroll and utilities. 
 
Five affirmative votes are required for passage after public comment.

UNFINISHED BUSINESS: 
  
 Order 66-26/27 Traffic Schedule Amendment RE: Lancaster Street - Sponsored by 
Sustainability & Transportation Committee, Councilor Regina Phillips, Chair 
    
  
The S&T Committee met on September 16, 2026 and unanimously voted to recommend 
changes to the traffic schedule on Lancaster St. There is an existing commercial loading 
zone that is currently underutilized. The designation of parking spaces would convert to 1 
hour time zone spaces and be included in the Portland High School approved parking 
spaces.
3 
This item must be read on two separate days. It received its first reading on October 19. 
Five affirmative votes are required for passage after public comment. 
    
 Order 67-26/27 Approving the Administrative Fee Increase for Parking in the First 
Light Commons Parking Lots - Sponsored by Sustainability & Transportation 
Committee, Councilor Regina Phillips, Chair 
    
  
The S&T Committee met on September 16, 2026 and unanimously voted to recommend a 
new parking rate structure in the parking lots adjacent to First Light Commons. The 
proposed rate would align with the rate of the city operated parking garages and provide 
10 free time zone spaces that will be included in residential zone 11.  
 
This item must be read on two separate days. It received its first reading on October 19. 
Five affirmative votes are required for passage after public comment. 
    
 Order 68-26/27 Approving the Appropriation of $350,000 from the Opioid 
Settlement Fund for Operation of Emergency Winter Warming Shelter - Sponsored 
by Danielle P. West, City Manager 
    
  
If passed, this Order would allocate $350,000 from the Opioid Settlement Fund to operate 
a 2026-2027 Winter Warming Shelter in Portland. This funding would be intended to 
supplement emergency winter warming shelter funding provided by the Maine State 
Housing Authority.  
 
Details regarding warming shelter operations, including location, will be finalized and 
published before the Council's consideration of this item on November 2, 2026. 
 
This item must be read on two separate days. It received its first reading on October 19. 
Five affirmative votes are required for passage after public comment. 
    
 Order 70-26/27 Approving the Appropriation of $900,000 from the Opioid 
Settlement Fund for Operation of Emergency Winter Warming Shelter at 166 
Riverside Industrial Parkway - Sponsored by Mark Dion, Mayor 
    
  
If passed, this Order would allocate $900,000 from the Opioid Settlement Fund to operate 
a 2026-2027 Winter Warming Shelter at 166 Riverside Industrial Parkway. This funding 
would be intended to supplement emergency winter warming shelter funding provided by 
the Maine State Housing Authority. 
 
This item must be read on two separate days. It received its first reading on October 26. 
Five affirmative votes are required for passage after public comment. 
    
ORDERS: 
  
 Order 74-26/27 Declaring a State of Limited Emergency at 654 Riverside Street - 
Sponsored by Mark Dion, Mayor 
    
  
If passed, this Order declares a limited state of emergency at the Homeless Services 
Center located at 654 Riverside Street for the 2026–2027 winter season. This temporary 
declaration expands shelter capacity by 50 beds through April 30, 2027, ensuring 
unhoused residents have access to emergency shelter during severe winter weather. 
 
Five affirmative votes are required for passage after public comment.
4 
 Order 75-26/27 Approving Option to Extend Northeast Air Ground Lease by 20-
Year Term Conditional on the Replacement of the Existing Hangar at a Minimum 
$4 Million Investment - Sponsored by Danielle P. West, City Manager 
    
  
The Portland International Jetport is requesting approval to issue a lease option to 
Northeast Air (NEA) for its northernmost ground lease.  The option would provide a 20-
year lease extension to the current ground lease conditional upon Northeast Air replacing 
an existing 50-year-old hangar on the leased premises and investing no less than $4 
million in the hangar replacement project. Northeast Air would be required to exercise the 
option within five years. 
 
Five affirmative votes are required for passage after public comment. 
    
 Order 76-26/27 Approving the Purchase and Sale Agreement Between Nordic Maine 
LLC and Portland RE: Portland Tehcnology Park Units 3 and 5 - Sponsored by 
Housing and Economic Development Committee, Councilor Pious Ali, Chair 
    
  
Staff presented a draft Purchase and Sale agreement to the Housing and Economic 
Development Committee at its meeting on October 6, 2026, resulting in a 4-0 vote to 
forward this to City Council with a recommendation of approval. 
 
The City created a seven-site land condominium at Portland Technology Park (PTP) and 
sold Unit 4 to Patrons Oxford Insurance Company in 2015, leaving six sites undeveloped. 
Earlier this year, City Council approved the Purchase and Sale Agreement on Unit 1 with 
Carassas Holdings, LLC, to develop the site into an incubator space and is still under 
contract.  
 
Offers to purchase Units 3 and 5 were received by the City in June 2026 and were 
brought to the Housing and Economic Development Committee for review. Based on 
guidance from the Committee on July 21, 2026, staff moved forward with an offer from 
Nordic Maine LLC. The intended use of Units 3 and 5 by Nordic Maine LLC is to 
develop the site into a Nordic-style spa featuring a hot pool, saunas, and cold plunges, 
along with indoor and outdoor spaces.  
 
Five affirmative votes are required for passage after public comment. 
    
 Order 77-26/27 Authorizing Salary Increase for Corporation Counsel - Sponsored 
by Mark Dion, Mayor 
    
  
If approved, this order would increase Corporation Counsel's annual salary to 
$202,738.20 effective retroactively from December 8, 2025.  
 
Five affirmative votes are required for passage after public comment. 
    
 
Order 78-26/27 Accepting and Appropriating and Additional $74,572.50 from the 
Land and Water Conservation Fund and Approving the Amendment to the Sub-
Grant Between Portland and the Maine Department of Agriculture, Conservation & 
Forestry RE: Riverton Trolley Park Improvements - Sponsored by Danielle P. West, 
City Manager 
    
  This item requests authorization to accept and appropriate an additional $74,572.50 in 
grant funding from the Land and Water Conservation Fund (LWCF) for ongoing
5 
improvements at Riverton Trolley Park. These supplemental funds will supplement the 
initial project allocation and support the continued enhancement of park infrastructure, 
recreation features, and public access. 
 
This item must be read on two separate days. This is its first reading. 
    
 
Order 79-26/27 Amending the Conditional Zone Agreement RE: Second 
Amendment to the Conditional Rezoning Agreement for Property in the Vicinity of 
St. Lawrence Arts/Congress Street - Sponsored by the Planning Board, Joseph 
Zamboni, Chair 
    
  
On October 27, 2026, the Planning Board held a public hearing and voted 6-0 (Messina 
absent) to recommend that the City Council adopt Hill Arts’ (“Applicant”) proposed 
amendments to Conditional Zoning Agreement C-58 for 76 Congress Street, with one 
modification: to further amend the proposal to include a 10-year time limit from the date 
of execution to the date of receiving a Certificate of Occupancy permit. The Board found 
that the amendments are consistent with the Comprehensive Plan for the City of Portland. 
As submitted, the amendments would allow minor modifications to the previously 
approved development, replacing the Parish Hall theater, reducing the overall proposal to 
a single 424-seat auditorium, and eliminating the agreement’s expiration date. 
 
This item must be read on two separate days. This is its first reading.
